source.prompt: A mountain lion (cougar, Puma concolor) of California, NOT an African lion, no mane, no spots. One adult male standing still, side-on neutral pose, four legs straight with clear gaps, big paws flat, head level. Realistic proportions: 75 cm at the shoulder, 1.3 m head and body, small round head, heavier neck and shoulders, long low muscular body, hindquarters a little higher than the shoulders, very long thick heavy tail (0.8 m) hanging low with the tip curving up. Plain tawny coat, cream muzzle, chin, throat and belly, black patches beside the muzzle, black backs of the ears, black tail tip. No base, no ground. Game-ready.

rig: quadruped template Q with a two-part tail: BODY, LEG_A (left fore + right hind), LEG_B, TAIL (inner half, pivot at the root), TAIL_TIP 8 (outer half, pivot mid-tail, child of TAIL in the one-level parent chain), HEAD (neck, head, ears; pivot at the neck base). Parts found from the geometry (tail cut at the rump and traced by edge distance, legs below the belly line with pivots there: elbow and stifle, head ahead of a plane at the neck base); weights blended over 5-10 cm. Parent pivots in extras.rig.

candidates.review: Good feline body, small head and a long J tail, but the head is turned to the side and the tail swings off the midline (asymmetric, against the brief's pitfalls), the forelegs stand crossed, and the tail is thinner. Prompt B (male) came back symmetric with the head level.

accuracy_notes: Generated (prompt B, the male), not adopted from a download: no CC0 cougar exists. Reads as a mountain lion: small round head, long low body with the hindquarters a little higher than the shoulders, big paws, a long heavy tail hanging in a J with a black tip, plain tawny coat with a darker back, cream muzzle, chin, throat, belly and inner legs, black whisker-base patches, black ear backs, pinkish nose, small golden eye. Whisker strands removed; legs below the belly 0.9x. Still wrong or unchecked: the generator sculpted ridged rings along the tail (geometry only; the colour is plain); the eyes are narrow lids, drawn as one golden face; the J of the tail reaches the ground before curling up, lower than a walking lion carries it; male proportions (heavier neck) on a 0.72 m animal. Check tail carriage, head size and the face marks against local trail-camera photos (brief C9).
